channel.title: Nature Communications
channel.description:
Nature Communications is an open access, multidisciplinary journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in all areas of the biological, health, physical, chemical and Earth sciences. Papers published by the journal aim to represent important advances of significance to specialists within each field.

We are committed to providing an efficient service for both authors and readers. Our team of independent editors make rapid and fair publication decisions. Prompt dissemination of accepted papers to a wide readership and beyond is achieved through a programme of continuous online publication.

item.title: Sparse X-ray spectro-tomography for high-sensitivity three-dimensional chemical imaging at the nanoscale
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77821-5

The study introduces a sparse spectro‑tomography method that cuts data needs in scanning mode by about two orders of magnitude, enabling high-sensitivity, low‑dose 3D chemical imaging. It uncovers surface Co reduction and Mn loss in battery particles, revealing key degradation pathways.
item.dc:title: Sparse X-ray spectro-tomography for high-sensitivity three-dimensional chemical imaging at the nanoscale

item.title: Practical synthesis of 3-Oxa/Aza-bicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes from 3-Oxa/Aza[3.1.1]propellanes
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76235-7

While bicyclo[1.1.1]pentanes (BCPs) and bicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes (BCHeps) serve as established 3D bioisosteres for para- and meta-substituted benzenes, accessible via ring-opening of their corresponding propellanes, the integration of heteroatoms into these propellane scaffolds has remained elusive. Herein, the authors report the practical synthesis of 3-oxa/aza[3.1.1]propellanes, two heteroatom-containing analogues of propellane, from 1,5-diiodo-3-hetero-BCHeps.
item.dc:title: Practical synthesis of 3-Oxa/Aza-bicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes from 3-Oxa/Aza[3.1.1]propellanes

item.title: Epithelial-mesenchymal Wnt crosstalk directs planar cell polarity in the developing cochlea
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77522-z

Patterning of cochlear hair cells is governed by planar cell polarity. Here, the authors show that multiple Wnt proteins from epithelial and mesenchymal compartments control cochlear elongation, hair cell patterning and core planar cell polarity proteins.
item.dc:title: Epithelial-mesenchymal Wnt crosstalk directs planar cell polarity in the developing cochlea

item.title: MAP2-mediated integrin dysregulation reprograms cancer cell plasticity in hepatocellular carcinoma
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77831-3

Cancer cell plasticity contributes to drug resistance and metastasis in liver cancer. Here, authors show that targeting MAP2 with estramustine phosphate disrupts cancer stemness and enhances sensitivity to sorafenib in hepatocellular carcinoma.
item.dc:title: MAP2-mediated integrin dysregulation reprograms cancer cell plasticity in hepatocellular carcinoma

item.title: Robust valley-polarized excitonic Mott states and doublons enabled by stacking-controlled moiré geometry
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77907-0

Stacking registry can reshape moiré exciton wavefunctions. Here, the authors show that H- and R-stacked WSe₂/WS₂ heterobilayers exhibit distinct intersite interaction strengths which control the robustness of a unit-filled exciton Mott state and the stability of doublons.
item.dc:title: Robust valley-polarized excitonic Mott states and doublons enabled by stacking-controlled moiré geometry

item.title: WLG coordinates multi-stress tolerance in rice by regulating DST-dependent H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub> homeostasis and stomatal aperture
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77791-8

Abiotic stresses reduce rice growth. Here, the authors show that E3 ubiquitin ligase WLG enhances tolerance to drought, salt, and heat via a molecular mechanism that increases guard cell hydrogen peroxide accumulation and limits water loss.
item.dc:title: WLG coordinates multi-stress tolerance in rice by regulating DST-dependent H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub> homeostasis and stomatal aperture

item.title: Laminar architecture of a decision circuit in the mouse orbitofrontal cortex
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77799-0

Economic choices rely on orbitofrontal cortex. The authors show that input and output variables are primarily encoded in superficial and deep layers, respectively, revealing a laminar organization in the decision circuit in mice.
item.dc:title: Laminar architecture of a decision circuit in the mouse orbitofrontal cortex

item.title: First principles reactive flux theory for surface reactions revealing multiple channels and recrossing dynamics
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77226-4

Heterogeneous reactions typically consist of multiple elementary steps whose rate coefficients help in elucidating the reaction mechanism. The authors combine metadynamics with a reactive flux approach to calculate rate coefficients of surface reactions, overcoming limitations of the transition state theory, and demonstrate application to CO oxidation on Pt(111) surfaces.
item.dc:title: First principles reactive flux theory for surface reactions revealing multiple channels and recrossing dynamics
